`dumps` and `loads` work through a `TimestampSigner`, under the salt `"django.core.signing"` unless they are given another; each may be given a key in place of `SECRET_KEY`, and `loads` old keys in place of `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` ([Signing: `Signer`, `TimestampSigner`, `dumps` and `loads`](signing.md)) (`django/core/signing.py:Signer.signature`, `django/core/signing.py:dumps`).

The sessions sign with `dumps`, but for the cache backend's: `SessionBase.encode` writes the stored data of the database, file and cached-database backends under the salt `"django.contrib.sessions.SessionStore"`, and the signed-cookie backend, which keeps the whole session in the cookie, signs it under `"django.contrib.sessions.backends.signed_cookies"` ([The session store: `SessionBase`](../auth/sessions.md), [The session backends](../auth/session-backends.md)) (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase.encode`, `django/contrib/sessions/backends/signed_cookies.py:SessionStore._get_session_key`).

`PasswordResetTokenGenerator` makes a reset token under the salt `"django.contrib.auth.tokens.PasswordResetTokenGenerator"`, with its own `PasswordResetTokenGenerator.secret` and `PasswordResetTokenGenerator.secret_fallbacks`, which are `SECRET_KEY` and `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` unless they are set ([Password reset: `PasswordResetTokenGenerator` and the reset views](../auth/password-reset.md#the-token-passwordresettokengenerator)) (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser._get_session_auth_hash`, `django/contrib/auth/tokens.py:PasswordResetTokenGenerator`).

`PasswordResetTokenGenerator` makes a reset token under the salt `"django.contrib.auth.tokens.PasswordResetTokenGenerator"`, with its own `PasswordResetTokenGenerator.secret` and `PasswordResetTokenGenerator.secret_fallbacks`, which are `SECRET_KEY` and `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS` unless they are set ([Password reset: `PasswordResetTokenGenerator` and the reset views](../auth/password-reset.md#the-token-passwordresettokengenerator)) (`django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:AbstractBaseUser._get_session_auth_hash`, `django/contrib/auth/tokens.py:PasswordResetTokenGenerator`).

`PasswordResetTokenGenerator.check_token` makes the token again under its secret and then under each of its fallbacks, and `get_user` makes the user's session hash again the same way, to compare with the one the session holds (`django/contrib/auth/tokens.py:PasswordResetTokenGenerator.check_token`, `django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:get_user`).

A key is changed in two steps, then: the new key into `SECRET_KEY` and the old one to the front of `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS`; and later the old one out of the list, which ends the sessions, reset tokens and other values it made (`docs/ref/settings.txt`).

4.1 added `SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS`, a list of old keys for rotating the key (`docs/releases/4.1.txt`); in 4.1 a rotation under the fallbacks still invalidated the sessions, a bug fixed in 4.1.8 (`docs/releases/4.1.8.txt`).

Under the cache backend the data is not signed and still holds the id, but the hash beside it, made under the old key, no longer matches the user's, and `get_user` flushes the session, deleting it and dropping its session key (`django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:get_user`, `django/contrib/sessions/backends/cache.py:SessionStore.load`).

A password's hash is made without it, with a salt the hasher draws for it, and a change of key leaves passwords as they were (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:BasePasswordHasher.salt`, `docs/ref/settings.txt`).

The PBKDF2 hashers, the default among them, make the hash with `pbkdf2`, which is `hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac` with SHA-256 unless another digest is given ([Password hashing: `make_password` and the hashers](../auth/hashers.md)) (`django/utils/crypto.py:pbkdf2`).
Salt, secret and value may each be a string or bytes: `force_bytes` makes them bytes (`django/utils/crypto.py:salted_hmac`).
Since 6.1 a call that names no algorithm warns, and in Django 2028 the default becomes `"sha256"` (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

Django 2028 is the release that was to be 7.0, named by its year under DEP 20, and the warning was renamed with it: RemovedInDjango70Warning in 6.1, `RemovedInDjango2028Warning` at this commit ([What still warns: the deprecations and the releases that end them](../changes/deprecations.md)) (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`, `deps:accepted/0020-annual-release-cycle.rst`).

It skips Django's own files, so it is reported at the innermost line outside Django that led to the call (`django/utils/crypto.py:salted_hmac`).
`base64_hmac` has the same deprecation and warns under its own name; it passes `"sha1"` on to `salted_hmac`, so a call of it warns once (`django/core/signing.py:base64_hmac`).

`constant_time_compare` makes both values bytes and returns what `secrets.compare_digest` says of them, a comparison that does not stop at the first difference: one that did would tell an attacker, by the time it took, how much of a guess was right (`django/utils/crypto.py:constant_time_compare`).

It is what `Signer.unsign`, `PasswordResetTokenGenerator.check_token`, the logging in and the loading of a request's user, the CSRF check ([The CSRF check: `CsrfViewMiddleware.process_view`](csrf-check.md)) and every password hasher but one compare with; `Argon2PasswordHasher` leaves the comparison to the argon2 library (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:Argon2PasswordHasher.verify`).

`get_random_string` makes a string of the length asked for, each character chosen by `secrets.choice` from the characters it is given: `RANDOM_STRING_CHARS`, the letters of both cases and the digits, unless it is given others (`django/utils/crypto.py:get_random_string`).

A string's strength in bits is the base-2 logarithm of the number of strings that could have been drawn: the CSRF secret, 32 of the 62 letters and digits, is about 190 bits (`django/middleware/csrf.py:_get_new_csrf_string`).

Among the other users are a session key, 32 of `VALID_KEY_CHARS`, lower-case letters and digits (`django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:SessionBase._get_new_session_key`), and the salts of the password hashers but the bcrypt ones (`django/contrib/auth/hashers.py:BasePasswordHasher.salt`).
